description_full: Whitecap Resources Inc. engages in the acquisition, development, and holding of interests in petroleum and natural gas properties and assets in Western Canada. Its primary areas of focus are development programs located in Northern Alberta, British Columbia, Central Alberta, and Western and Eastern Saskatchewan. The company was founded in 2009 and is headquartered in Calgary, Canada.

financial_summary: Whitecap Resources, Inc. is a large-cap energy business with a $14.4B market cap on $4.2B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory. Operating margins are contracting by -5.9pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.

Returns on capital run at 11% against a 8% cost of capital, a 3-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it. Gross margins of 61% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $431M in free cash flow — roughly 10 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.73× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -8.8% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.3× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 8.3×.

Shareholder yield of 4.6% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 1.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
